scope: Sources support the named teaching concepts. Patient facts, dialogue, and timelines are newly authored fiction. This is not a systematic evidence review, source-integrity audit, or verification of local policy. No paper-specific outcome or effect-size claims are made.

sources.title: NIMH — Understanding Psychosis
sources.location: What causes psychosis?; How is psychosis treated?; coordinated specialty care components
sources.supports: Psychosis has multiple possible causes; early care can combine medication, psychotherapy, family work, practical support, and education or employment goals.
sources.supportingExcerpt: There is no one cause of psychosis.
sources.access: Primary agency HTML opened; relevant sections read.

sources.title: NICE CG178 — Psychosis and schizophrenia in adults
sources.location: First episode psychosis; Choice of antipsychotic medication; How to use antipsychotic medication
sources.supports: Shared medication choice, baseline and continuing adverse-effect monitoring, and recognition that akathisia can resemble agitation or anxiety.
sources.supportingExcerpt: the overlap between akathisia and agitation or anxiety
sources.access: Relevant primary-source recommendation text retrieved through indexed search. Direct full-page opening returned HTTP 403.

sources.title: NICE NG222 — Depression in adults: treatment and management
sources.location: Recognition and assessment; Antidepressant medication for people at risk of suicide
sources.supports: Assessment includes functional impact, illness course, coexisting disorders, and mood-elevation history; treatment follow-up includes safety and adverse effects.
sources.supportingExcerpt: any history of mood elevation (to determine if the depression may be part of bipolar disorder)
sources.access: Relevant primary-source recommendation text retrieved through indexed search. Direct full-page opening returned HTTP 403.

sources.title: NICE NG225 — Self-harm: assessment, management and preventing recurrence
sources.location: Risk assessment tools and scales; recommendations 1.11.7–1.11.8 on safety planning
sources.supports: Limits of risk scales as prediction or disposition tools; collaborative safety planning, support contacts, and addressing access to lethal means.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Do not use risk assessment tools and scales to predict future suicide or repetition of self-harm.
sources.scopeLimit: This guideline's population is people who self-harm. Leah reports suicidal ideation without a confirmed act; applying its general safety-planning principles to her vignette is an educational extrapolation requiring faculty review. It does not establish local policy or supersede a local suicide-assessment framework.
sources.access: Relevant primary-source recommendation text retrieved through indexed search. Direct full-page opening returned HTTP 403.
sources.resolution: Accepted as an educational extrapolation: Leah-01/05 teach collaborative safety planning and lethal-means reduction (now naming firearms and the new prescription) as supervised tasks, and the chapter text states that the supervising clinician and local policy decide disposition. No local suicide-assessment framework is replaced. Approved by the requesting author 2026-10-04.

sources.title: ASAM — Alcohol Withdrawal Management Guideline
sources.supports: Withdrawal management is part of engaging a person in ongoing alcohol-use-disorder care, rather than the entirety of treatment.
sources.supportingExcerpt: alcohol withdrawal management alone is not an effective treatment for alcohol use disorder
sources.access: Primary society HTML opened. This draft uses its scope statement, not a reproduced dosing or level-of-care algorithm.

sources.title: NIAAA — Alcohol Use Disorder: From Risk to Diagnosis to Recovery
sources.location: How is alcohol withdrawal managed?; How is AUD treated?
sources.supports: Withdrawal can include tremor, sweating, autonomic change, and serious complications; medical assessment and continuing behavioral or medication treatment are distinct needs.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Treatment and continuing care for AUD are measured in months and sometimes years
sources.access: Primary agency HTML opened; relevant sections read.

sources.title: VA National Center for PTSD — Treatment of Co-Occurring PTSD and Substance Use Disorder
sources.supports: Offer care for both PTSD and substance use disorder; one condition should not automatically block treatment for the other. No comparative efficacy or study-outcome claim is made in the draft.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Having one should not be a barrier to receiving treatment for the other.
sources.access: Primary agency HTML opened; guideline-based key points read.

sources.title: NICE CG103 — Delirium: prevention, diagnosis and management
sources.location: Indicators of delirium; assessment and diagnosis; treating delirium; if delirium does not resolve
sources.supports: Assess acute fluctuating changes, investigate contributors, use supportive care, and reassess persistent cognitive concerns. Medication decisions need individual review.
sources.supportingExcerpt: identify and manage the possible underlying cause or combination of causes
sources.access: Relevant primary-source recommendation text retrieved through indexed search. Direct full-page opening returned HTTP 403; the NCBI copy required a browser check. Full recommendation review remains a faculty-review task.

sources.title: AMA Code of Medical Ethics 2.1.2 — Decisions for Adult Patients Who Lack Capacity
sources.location: Patient participation; identifying a surrogate; substituted judgment; institutional consultation
sources.supports: Support participation despite impairment and identify a surrogate through applicable law and policy rather than family presence alone.
sources.supportingExcerpt: in keeping with applicable law and policy
sources.scopeLimit: Ethics guidance does not determine Maine law, a site's detention procedures, or learner privileges.
sources.access: Primary society HTML opened; the opinion read.
sources.resolution: Accepted: Marisol-04 asks the learner to verify surrogate authority under local policy and the disclaimer now states the case does not determine detention or surrogate authority (C10). Maine-specific statute text is held for a verified citation (localNote, schema only). Approved by the requesting author 2026-10-04.

sources.title: AMA Code of Medical Ethics 2.1.1 — Informed Consent
sources.location: Patient abilities, explanation of alternatives, and documentation
sources.supports: Assess understanding and implications of alternatives, provide understandable information, and document the decision-making conversation.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Assess the patient’s ability to understand relevant medical information
sources.scopeLimit: The four-abilities teaching framework in Marisol chapter 4 also reuses the existing library capacity module's approach; this opinion is not presented as a statutory capacity test.
sources.access: Primary society HTML opened; the opinion read.
sources.resolution: Accepted: the four-abilities framework in Marisol-04 reuses the library capacity module and is presented as a teaching approach, not a statutory test; the chapter links the Decisional Capacity tool. Approved by the requesting author 2026-10-04.
